toc.topic: Pre-Assessment (Prerequisites)

data.Topic: Pre-Assessment (Prerequisites)
data.Sub Topic: Baseline readiness check covering all prerequisite areas before the program begins — see the Prerequisites & Audience sheet for the full list. Confirms starting proficiency; does not gate attendance on its own.
data.Learning Outcomes: Baseline readiness confirmed across all prerequisite areas; any gaps are flagged for pre-work before Day 1.

toc.topic: Program Orientation

data.Topic: Program Orientation
data.Sub Topic: Program kickoff: introduce the Meridian Financial Group case study and the full program journey, walk through the curriculum structure, Milestone / Interview Bot / Capstone checkpoints, tooling and environment setup, and readiness criteria; address questions before Day 1 begins.
data.Learning Outcomes: The program structure is understood, tooling access is confirmed, and expectations are clear before Day 1.

toc.topic: Data Architecture Thinking & Pattern Selection

data.Topic: Data Architecture Thinking & Pattern Selection
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn to think and design at the platform level rather than the pipeline level. The session walks through the major data-platform architecture patterns used today -- batch warehousing, streaming/event-driven pipelines, the lakehouse pattern and data mesh -- comparing their strengths, trade-offs and best-fit scenarios with real examples. Participants then practice selecting and justifying the right pattern combination for a real business scenario, instead of defaulting to whichever pattern they already know best.
data.Hands-on Activity: Kick off Meridian Financial Group — Customer 360 & Analytics Platform: review the business brief for the Customer 360 platform (Account, Transaction, Interaction and Product data sources), select a data-architecture pattern combination, and document an initial system context diagram.
data.Learning Outcomes: Pattern-selection brief and system context diagram (v1) opening the Meridian Financial Group architecture package.

toc.topic: Data NFRs & Fitness Functions

data.Topic: Data NFRs & Fitness Functions
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to turn business expectations -- such as 'customer data must be queryable within seconds of an interaction' or 'transaction records must never be lost' -- into specific, measurable targets for throughput, freshness, consistency and durability. The session then shows how to encode these targets as automated checks, called fitness functions, that run continuously and flag the platform the moment it drifts from what was promised, rather than the problem being discovered only after a report goes wrong.
data.Hands-on Activity: Using the context diagram from the previous session, define data NFRs for the Transaction data source (freshness, throughput, durability targets) and draft one executable fitness function to guard the highest-priority NFR in the data pipeline.
data.Learning Outcomes: Data NFR specification and fitness-function sketch appended to the Meridian Financial Group architecture package.

toc.topic: Architecture Decision Records & Review Practice

data.Topic: Architecture Decision Records & Review Practice
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to document and communicate the reasoning behind a data architecture decision using an industry-standard format called an Architecture Decision Record (ADR), so anyone joining the project later can understand why a choice was made without having to ask around. The session also covers how to run a structured peer design review -- similar to a code review, but for architecture -- so decisions are challenged and validated by others before they are locked in, rather than approved informally.
data.Hands-on Activity: Formalize the pattern decision from Session 1 as an Architecture Decision Record, then run a structured peer review of the data NFRs defined in Session 2 and log the review outcomes.
data.Learning Outcomes: ADR-001 and a peer-review log added to the Meridian Financial Group architecture package.

toc.topic: Capacity Planning, Performance Diagnosis & Pipeline Resilience

data.Topic: Capacity Planning, Performance Diagnosis & Pipeline Resilience
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to estimate, before a pipeline goes live, whether it will hold up under real-world data volume -- for example, how many transaction events it can ingest per second before it falls behind -- and how to spot likely bottlenecks such as a slow join, an undersized cluster or a skewed partition. The session then introduces Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), a structured way of asking 'what could go wrong here, and how bad would it be?' for every stage of the pipeline. Participants use the answers to design resilience patterns -- such as replay queues, dead-letter handling and checkpointing -- so that when something does fail, the pipeline recovers cleanly instead of silently losing or duplicating data.
data.Hands-on Activity: Build a capacity model and performance budget for the Transaction data pipeline using the NFRs from Session 2, then run a Failure Mode and Effects Analysis against the same pipeline and design resilience patterns for the top failure modes identified.
data.Learning Outcomes: Capacity model, FMEA worksheet and resilience pattern map, all scoped to the Transaction data pipeline.

toc.topic: Case Lab: End-to-End Data Platform Architecture Design

data.Topic: Case Lab: End-to-End Data Platform Architecture Design
data.Sub Topic: This is a consolidation session. Participants bring together everything produced across the module -- the pattern decision, the NFRs, the ADR, the capacity model and the resilience plan -- into a single, coherent end-to-end architecture document for the case-study platform. Participants then present this design to their peers and respond to questions and challenges, practicing how to defend a design decision under scrutiny, the way they would in a real client or leadership review.
data.Hands-on Activity: Combine the pattern decision, NFRs, ADR, capacity model and resilience plan from Sessions 1-4 into the complete Meridian Financial Group Customer 360 distributed-system design, and present it for peer critique.
data.Learning Outcomes: Consolidated Meridian Financial Group architecture design package (v1) -- the baseline every later module builds on.

toc.topic: LLM Integration Patterns for Data Platforms & Responsible AI Checkpoints

data.Topic: LLM Integration Patterns for Data Platforms & Responsible AI Checkpoints
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn the common patterns for adding an AI-powered capability -- such as a natural-language data-query assistant or an AI-assisted cataloging tool -- into an existing data platform: where it plugs in, what data it needs, and how it communicates with the rest of the platform. Alongside this, the session introduces responsible-AI checkpoints -- practical questions the team should ask before building an AI feature over customer data, covering data privacy, bias and misuse risk -- so governance is built in from day one rather than added as an afterthought.
data.Hands-on Activity: Using the Meridian Financial Group architecture package, identify where a proposed natural-language analytics assistant fits into the existing Customer 360 design, map the integration pattern, and add a responsible-AI checklist to the existing ADR log.
data.Learning Outcomes: LLM integration-point diagram and responsible-AI checklist appended to the Meridian Financial Group architecture package.

toc.topic: RAG & Vector Search Architecture over Enterprise Data

data.Topic: RAG & Vector Search Architecture over Enterprise Data
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to design a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with vector search -- a widely used way of making an AI feature answer questions using a company's own data (like customer transaction history) instead of only what the AI model already knows. The session compares the three main ways to customize an AI model's behaviour -- fine-tuning, prompt engineering and RAG -- and teaches participants how to choose the right one based on cost, how often the underlying data changes, and how accurate the answers need to be.
data.Hands-on Activity: Design a RAG pipeline with vector search over the Meridian Financial Group customer-interaction history to power the natural-language analytics assistant scoped in the previous session, and justify a customization strategy against the platform's freshness and cost constraints.
data.Learning Outcomes: RAG architecture design and customization trade-off decision appended to the Meridian Financial Group package.

toc.topic: Agentic Data Workflows & AI Cost Economics

data.Topic: Agentic Data Workflows & AI Cost Economics
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to design an 'agentic' AI workflow for a data platform -- one where the AI does not just answer a single question but carries out a short sequence of steps on the user's behalf, such as checking a customer's transaction history and then flagging a data-quality issue for review. The session also covers how to estimate what an AI feature will actually cost to run once real users are using it at scale, so the business can make an informed decision before committing budget to the feature.
data.Hands-on Activity: Extend the RAG design from the previous session into a lightweight agentic workflow covering customer lookup and data-quality flagging, and estimate monthly AI spend for the Meridian Financial Group platform at three usage scales.
data.Learning Outcomes: Agent architecture diagram and cost model, both scoped to the same analytics-assistant feature.

toc.topic: AI Evaluation, Observability & Governance for Data Features

data.Topic: AI Evaluation, Observability & Governance for Data Features
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to keep an AI feature trustworthy after it goes live, not just at launch. The session covers how to test AI responses for accuracy before release, how to monitor an AI feature in production -- tracking things like response speed and how often it gives an incorrect or made-up answer about a customer's data -- and how to set up automatic guardrails that catch a decline in quality before business users notice it.
data.Hands-on Activity: Define the evaluation and observability plan -- offline/online evaluation, latency and hallucination-rate monitoring, regression gates -- for the Meridian Financial Group analytics-assistant feature built across Sessions 1-3.
data.Learning Outcomes: Evaluation and observability plan for the analytics-assistant feature.

toc.topic: Case Lab: AI-Integrated Data Feature Assembly

data.Topic: Case Lab: AI-Integrated Data Feature Assembly
data.Sub Topic: This is a consolidation session for the AI workstream. Participants combine the integration design, the RAG pipeline, the agentic workflow and the evaluation plan from the previous four sessions into one complete, presentable design for the AI-powered feature, and walk their peers through it for feedback -- the same way they would present a feature design to a product or engineering leadership team.
data.Hands-on Activity: Combine the integration pattern, RAG design, agentic workflow and evaluation plan from Sessions 1-4 into one complete AI-integrated feature design for Meridian Financial Group, and present it for peer critique.
data.Learning Outcomes: Consolidated AI-integrated feature design package (v1), layered onto the Module 1 architecture package.

toc.topic: Well-Architected Review & Multi-Service Cloud Data Platform Design

data.Topic: Well-Architected Review & Multi-Service Cloud Data Platform Design
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to run a Well-Architected review -- a structured checklist, used across all major cloud providers, that examines a design for cost efficiency, security, reliability and performance before it is built. Using the outcome of that review, participants then design how the data platform will actually be laid out across multiple cloud services -- ingestion, storage, warehouse/lakehouse compute and orchestration -- working together, rather than treating cloud deployment as a single black box.
data.Hands-on Activity: Run a Well-Architected review against the Meridian Financial Group design produced in Modules 1-2, then design the multi-service cloud topology -- ingestion, storage and compute -- that will host the platform, including the AI-integrated feature.
data.Learning Outcomes: Well-Architected trade-off analysis and multi-service cloud architecture diagram for Meridian Financial Group.

toc.topic: Infrastructure as Code for Data Platforms

data.Topic: Infrastructure as Code for Data Platforms
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to turn a cloud data-platform architecture diagram into Infrastructure as Code (IaC) -- reusable, version-controlled scripts that create the pipelines, storage and warehouse environment automatically and consistently every time, instead of engineers manually clicking through a cloud console. This makes environments repeatable, auditable and far faster to stand up or tear down.
data.Hands-on Activity: Translate the cloud architecture diagram from the previous session into a golden-path Infrastructure-as-Code template for the Meridian Financial Group platform.
data.Learning Outcomes: Infrastructure-as-Code template scoped to the Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Multi-Region Resilience & Release Strategy for Data Platforms

data.Topic: Multi-Region Resilience & Release Strategy for Data Platforms
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to design a data platform so it can survive the failure of an entire cloud region -- for example, if a whole data centre goes offline -- including setting clear recovery targets for how much data the business can afford to lose and how quickly the platform must be back online. The session also covers release strategy: how to roll out new versions of a pipeline or schema safely, with the ability to roll back instantly if something goes wrong.
data.Hands-on Activity: Design a multi-region disaster-recovery strategy and a release/rollback plan for the Meridian Financial Group platform, building directly on the Infrastructure-as-Code baseline from the previous session.
data.Learning Outcomes: Disaster-recovery strategy and release plan for the Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Case Lab: Data Platform Reliability & Cost Optimization

data.Topic: Case Lab: Data Platform Reliability & Cost Optimization
data.Sub Topic: This is a consolidation session for the cloud workstream. Participants bring together the cloud architecture, the Infrastructure-as-Code setup and the disaster-recovery/release plan into a single platform reliability plan, and add a cost-optimization pass -- identifying where the platform is over-provisioned or paying for storage/compute capacity it does not need.
data.Hands-on Activity: Combine the cloud architecture, Infrastructure-as-Code baseline and disaster-recovery/release plan from Sessions 1-3 into an end-to-end platform reliability plan for Meridian Financial Group, including a cost-optimization pass.
data.Learning Outcomes: Consolidated cloud deployment package (v1), layered onto the architecture and AI-feature packages.

toc.topic: Data Security Architecture & Vulnerability Management

data.Topic: Data Security Architecture & Vulnerability Management
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to build security into the data platform itself -- deciding upfront how data will be encrypted at rest and in transit, and who is allowed to access which datasets -- rather than adding security as an afterthought. The session also covers how to run a basic vulnerability assessment against a data platform to identify its weak points, and how to set up a workflow for fixing what is found, so vulnerability management becomes an ongoing habit rather than a one-time audit.
data.Hands-on Activity: Thread-model the Meridian Financial Group platform as designed across Modules 1-3, identify the highest-priority vulnerabilities, and draft a remediation plan for the same architecture.
data.Learning Outcomes: Threat model and remediation plan for the Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Zero Trust & Identity-Centric Design for Data Access

data.Topic: Zero Trust & Identity-Centric Design for Data Access
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn Zero Trust: the principle that no request should be trusted by default, even if it comes from inside the company network, and every access request to a dataset must be verified based on identity. The session teaches participants how to redesign an existing data platform's access boundaries around this principle -- including row- and column-level access control -- moving away from the older idea of a single secure 'perimeter' wrapped around the whole platform.
data.Hands-on Activity: Redesign the Meridian Financial Group platform's access boundaries using zero-trust principles, building directly on the threat model from the previous session.
data.Learning Outcomes: Zero-trust design for the Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Regulatory Compliance & Continuous Compliance Automation

data.Topic: Regulatory Compliance & Continuous Compliance Automation
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to map relevant regulatory requirements -- such as data-privacy or financial-services-specific rules -- directly onto the data platform, so compliance is designed in rather than checked at the end. The session also covers how to automate at least one compliance check, such as automatically verifying that sensitive customer fields are encrypted or masked, so evidence of compliance is collected continuously instead of scrambled together during an annual audit.
data.Hands-on Activity: Map relevant compliance requirements onto the Meridian Financial Group architecture and automate one control check as a continuous compliance safeguard.
data.Learning Outcomes: Compliance mapping and one automated control check for the Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Case Lab: Secure & Governed Data Architecture Review

data.Topic: Case Lab: Secure & Governed Data Architecture Review
data.Sub Topic: This is a consolidation session for the security and governance workstream. Participants bring together the threat model, the zero-trust redesign and the compliance mapping into one complete secure-architecture review, and produce a prioritized roadmap listing which security and governance gaps need to be fixed first and why -- the kind of document a security or compliance lead would expect to see before sign-off.
data.Hands-on Activity: Consolidate the threat model, zero-trust design and compliance mapping from Sessions 1-3 into a full secure-architecture review of Meridian Financial Group, and present a remediation roadmap.
data.Learning Outcomes: Consolidated security and governance package (v1), layered onto the cumulative Meridian Financial Group design.

toc.topic: Translating Data Architecture to Business Language & Influence Without Authority

data.Topic: Translating Data Architecture to Business Language & Influence Without Authority
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to explain data-architecture decisions and trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders -- leadership, product managers, clients -- in language they can act on, without oversimplifying or losing important nuance. The session also covers how to negotiate for a technical priority, such as extra time to close a data-quality gap, when the participant has no formal authority over the other team, through a realistic negotiation role-play.
data.Hands-on Activity: Build a stakeholder pitch for the complete Meridian Financial Group platform -- architecture, AI feature, cloud deployment and security posture -- and rehearse a negotiation for one contested trade-off with a peer playing a resistant stakeholder.
data.Learning Outcomes: Stakeholder pitch deck and negotiation notes for the complete Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Cost/ROI Framing & Change Leadership

data.Topic: Cost/ROI Framing & Change Leadership
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn how to present a technical decision in the terms the business cares about most -- cost and return on investment -- rather than purely technical merit. The session also covers change leadership: how to plan and sequence the rollout of a new data platform or process in a way that anticipates resistance from the teams affected by the change, instead of assuming everyone will adopt it automatically.
data.Hands-on Activity: Build a cost/ROI one-pager for the Meridian Financial Group platform and a phased rollout plan for taking it into production.
data.Learning Outcomes: ROI one-pager and phased rollout plan for the Meridian Financial Group platform.

toc.topic: Build vs Buy & Vendor Evaluation

data.Topic: Build vs Buy & Vendor Evaluation
data.Sub Topic: Participants learn a structured framework for deciding whether to build a data-platform capability in-house or buy it from a vendor -- weighing cost, time-to-market, control and long-term maintenance -- instead of defaulting to whichever option the team is most comfortable with. The session also covers how to run a basic vendor evaluation, comparing options against the same criteria side by side.
data.Hands-on Activity: Apply a build-vs-buy scoring framework to one Meridian Financial Group component -- the analytics-assistant vendor-vs-in-house decision -- completing the Meridian Financial Group evidence pack.
data.Learning Outcomes: Build-vs-buy scorecard, completing the final version of the Meridian Financial Group evidence pack.

toc.topic: Capstone Day 1 — Architect the Platform

data.Topic: Capstone Day 1 — Architect the Platform
data.Sub Topic: Use Case: Harborview Logistics — Supply Chain Data Platform — a supply chain data platform (shipment tracking, warehouse inventory, carrier performance and demand-forecasting data) that the learner has not worked on during the program. Apply the architecture-practice skill set independently: pattern selection, non-functional requirements, Architecture Decision Records and a distributed-system design, on a new platform and without step-by-step guidance.
data.Hands-on Activity: Independently architect the Harborview Logistics platform end to end: select an architecture pattern combination, define NFRs, write the supporting ADRs, and produce a distributed-system design for the core supply-chain data flow.
data.Learning Outcomes: Harborview Logistics architecture design package: pattern decision, NFR specification, ADR set and system design.

toc.topic: Capstone Day 2 — Integrate AI & Deploy to Cloud

data.Topic: Capstone Day 2 — Integrate AI & Deploy to Cloud
data.Sub Topic: Extend the Day 1 architecture with an AI-powered demand-forecasting assistant and deploy the resulting platform to the cloud using Infrastructure as Code, applying the AI-integration and cloud-deployment skill sets independently to the new platform.
data.Hands-on Activity: Design and integrate an AI-powered demand-forecasting assistant into the Day 1 architecture, then translate the resulting platform into a multi-service cloud design and an Infrastructure-as-Code deployment baseline.
data.Learning Outcomes: AI-integrated feature design and cloud deployment package for the Harborview Logistics platform.

toc.topic: Capstone Day 3 — Secure, Comply & Build the Business Case

data.Topic: Capstone Day 3 — Secure, Comply & Build the Business Case
data.Sub Topic: Secure the platform built on Days 1-2, map it against relevant compliance requirements, and build the stakeholder business case, applying the security and business-translation skill sets independently to close out the capstone build.
data.Hands-on Activity: Thread-model and secure the Harborview Logistics platform, map it against relevant compliance requirements, and build the stakeholder pitch and cost/ROI case for taking it into production.
data.Learning Outcomes: Security and compliance package plus stakeholder pitch and ROI case for the Harborview Logistics platform.

toc.topic: Capstone Evaluation & Panel Review

data.Topic: Capstone Evaluation & Panel Review
data.Sub Topic: Participants present the complete Harborview Logistics capstone -- covering architecture, AI integration, cloud deployment, security and the business case -- to a review panel made up of the trainer and, where available, a client-side stakeholder. Participants respond to panel questions and defend their design decisions, the same way they would in a real project sign-off or client review.
data.Hands-on Activity: Deliver an end-to-end walkthrough of the Harborview Logistics capstone to a panel (trainer and, where available, a client-side stakeholder); respond to panel questioning on architecture, AI-integration, cloud, security and business-case decisions.
data.Learning Outcomes: Panel-scored capstone evaluation, covering design command, trade-off articulation and completeness of the evidence pack.
